Stage 5: Pretraining

Lecture 32: Stage 5 Capstone — Pretrained Text Generator

A Complete System: Pretrained Model, Multiple Generation Strategies, Quality Evaluation, and Interactive Playground

~50 min read | Capstone | You built a language model from scratch. Now watch it speak.

Introduction: The Culmination

In the Stage 4 Capstone (Lecture 24), you built the Mini GPT-2 architecture — but with random weights, it could only produce gibberish. Now, after building the entire training machinery, you will see a model you built and trained from scratch generating text that resembles real language patterns. This is how ChatGPT, Claude, and every LLM works. The difference is only scale.

What You Will Build: A pretrained Mini GPT-2 with four generation strategies (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p), quality evaluation metrics, and an interactive generation playground.

Part 1: Pretraining with Extended Corpus

We use a corpus with varied sentence structures and enough repetition for our small model to learn meaningful patterns.

Python 

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ============================================================
# STAGE 5 CAPSTONE: PRETRAINED TEXT GENERATOR
# ============================================================

class CharTok:
    def __init__(self, text):
        ch = sorted(set(text))
        self.c2i={c:i for i,c in enumerate(ch)}
        self.i2c={i:c for i,c in enumerate(ch)}
        self.V=len(ch)
    def encode(self,t): return [self.c2i.get(c,0) for c in t]
    def decode(self,ids): return ''.join(self.i2c.get(i,'?') for i in ids)

class LN:
    def __init__(self,d):self.g=np.ones(d);self.b=np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self,x):
        mu=x.mean(-1,keepdims=True);v=x.var(-1,keepdims=True)
        return self.g*((x-mu)/np.sqrt(v+1e-5))+self.b
class Attn:
    def __init__(self,d,h,s):
        self.h=h;self.hd=d//h
        self.Wq=np.random.randn(d,d)*s;self.Wk=np.random.randn(d,d)*s
        self.Wv=np.random.randn(d,d)*s;self.Wo=np.random.randn(d,d)*s
    def forward(self,x):
        B,T,C=x.shape;h=self.h;hd=self.hd
        Q=(x@self.Wq).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K=(x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V=(x@self.Wv).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        sc=Q@K.transpose(0,1,3,2)/np.sqrt(hd)
        sc+=np.triu(np.ones((T,T)),k=1)*(-1e9)
        e=np.exp(sc-sc.max(-1,keepdims=True));a=e/e.sum(-1,keepdims=True)
        return(a@V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(B,T,C)@self.Wo
class FFN:
    def __init__(self,d,s):
        df=4*d;self.W1=np.random.randn(d,df)*s;self.b1=np.zeros(df)
        self.W2=np.random.randn(df,d)*s;self.b2=np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self,x):
        z=x@self.W1+self.b1
        return(0.5*z*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(z+0.044715*z**3))))@self.W2+self.b2
class Blk:
    def __init__(self,d,h,s):
        self.ln1=LN(d);self.at=Attn(d,h,s);self.ln2=LN(d);self.ff=FFN(d,s)
    def forward(self,x):
        x=x+self.at.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
        x=x+self.ff.forward(self.ln2.forward(x));return x
class GPT:
    def __init__(self,V,d,h,L,T):
        s=0.02;rs=s/np.sqrt(2*L)
        self.tok=np.random.randn(V,d)*s;self.pos=np.random.randn(T,d)*s
        self.blocks=[Blk(d,h,rs) for _ in range(L)]
        self.ln_f=LN(d);self.head=np.random.randn(d,V)*s;self.V=V;self.T=T
    def forward(self,ids):
        B,T=ids.shape;x=self.tok[ids]+self.pos[:T]
        for bl in self.blocks:x=bl.forward(x)
        return self.ln_f.forward(x)@self.head

def cross_entropy(logits,targets):
    B,T,V=logits.shape;lf=logits.reshape(B*T,V);tf=targets.reshape(B*T)
    s=lf-lf.max(-1,keepdims=True)
    lp=s-np.log(np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True))
    return -lp[np.arange(B*T),tf].mean()

def train_step(model,inp,tgt,lr):
    logits=model.forward(inp);loss=cross_entropy(logits,tgt)
    B,T,V=logits.shape
    s=logits-logits.max(-1,keepdims=True)
    p=np.exp(s)/np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
    oh=np.zeros_like(p)
    for b in range(B):
        for t in range(T):oh[b,t,tgt[b,t]]=1.0
    dl=(p-oh)/(B*T)
    x=model.tok[inp]+model.pos[:T]
    for bl in model.blocks:x=bl.forward(x)
    x=model.ln_f.forward(x)
    dh=np.zeros_like(model.head)
    for b in range(B):dh+=x[b].T@dl[b]
    gn=np.sqrt((dh**2).sum())
    if gn>1:dh/=gn
    model.head-=lr*dh
    de=np.zeros_like(model.tok);dx=dl@model.head.T
    for b in range(B):
        for t in range(T):de[inp[b,t]]+=dx[b,t]
    en=np.sqrt((de**2).sum())
    if en>1:de/=en
    model.tok-=lr*de
    return loss

# === TRAINING CORPUS ===
corpus = """the cat sat on the mat and looked around the room.
the dog ran in the park and played with the ball.
a bird flew over the tree and sang a beautiful song.
the sun shone brightly in the clear blue sky today.
the model learns to predict the next word in text.
a neural network processes data through many layers.
the attention mechanism helps focus on important parts.
training a language model requires lots of text data.
the transformer block combines attention and feed forward.
each layer builds on the output of the previous one.
the loss function measures how well the model predicts.
gradient descent updates weights to reduce the total loss.
the learning rate controls how big each update step is.
pretraining teaches the model to understand language patterns.
the cat sat on the mat and watched the birds outside.
the dog ran in the park and chased the other dogs.
""" * 4

tok = CharTok(corpus)
ids = tok.encode(corpus)
T = 32
data = []
for i in range(0,len(ids)-T,12):
    ch=ids[i:i+T+1]
    if len(ch)==T+1:data.append((np.array(ch[:-1]),np.array(ch[1:])))

model = GPT(tok.V, d=64, h=4, L=4, T=T)
print("=" * 58)
print("  CAPSTONE: PRETRAINING MINI GPT-2")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Vocab: {tok.V} | Tokens: {len(ids)} | Examples: {len(data)}")

max_steps=100; bs=8; max_lr=0.005; min_lr=0.0005; warmup=15
losses=[]
for step in range(max_steps):
    idx=np.random.choice(len(data),bs)
    inp=np.stack([data[i][0] for i in idx])
    tgt=np.stack([data[i][1] for i in idx])
    if step {losses[-1]:.4f} ({(1-losses[-1]/losses[0])*100:.1f}% improvement)")
print("\\n  Sample generations:")
for prompt in ["the ", "a ", "the model "]:
    print(f"  '{prompt}' -> '{prompt}{gen(prompt,60,0.6)}'")
print(f"\\n  Model ready for generation experiments!")

Part 2: Generation Strategies

A language model produces a probability distribution over the vocabulary at each step. How we choose a token dramatically affects output quality. The four main strategies:

  • Greedy: Always pick the highest-probability token. Deterministic but often repetitive.
  • Temperature: Divide logits by T before softmax. T<1 = sharper (confident); T>1 = flatter (random).
  • Top-k: Only consider the k most probable tokens, renormalize, sample. Prevents long-tail noise. GPT-2 default: k=40.
  • Top-p (Nucleus): Include smallest token set whose cumulative probability exceeds p. Adapts dynamically to confidence. Default in Claude, GPT-4, and most modern APIs.
Python 

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ============================================================
# FOUR GENERATION STRATEGIES - Implementation & Comparison
# ============================================================

def sm(logits):
    s=logits-logits.max();e=np.exp(s);return e/e.sum()
def greedy(lo):return int(np.argmax(lo))
def temp_sample(lo,T=0.8):p=sm(lo/max(T,1e-8));return int(np.random.choice(len(p),p=p))
def topk_sample(lo,k=10,T=0.8):
    sc=lo/max(T,1e-8);top=np.argsort(sc)[-k:];f=np.full_like(sc,-1e9);f[top]=sc[top]
    p=sm(f);return int(np.random.choice(len(p),p=p))
def topp_sample(lo,p_th=0.9,T=0.8):
    p=sm(lo/max(T,1e-8));si=np.argsort(p)[::-1];cs=np.cumsum(p[si])
    cut=np.searchsorted(cs,p_th)+1;ni=si[:cut];np_=p[ni];np_/=np_.sum()
    return int(np.random.choice(ni,p=np_))

# Simulate realistic logits
V=50;logits=np.random.randn(V)*0.5
logits[10]=3.0;logits[25]=2.5;logits[30]=2.0;logits[5]=1.5
probs=sm(logits);top5=np.argsort(probs)[-5:][::-1]

print("="*58)
print("  GENERATION STRATEGIES COMPARISON")
print("="*58)
print("\\n  Top 5 tokens by probability:")
for i,idx in enumerate(top5):
    print(f"    {i+1}. Token {idx}: {probs[idx]:.4f} ({probs[idx]*100:.1f}%)")

from collections import Counter
strats={'Greedy':lambda l:greedy(l),'Temp=0.5':lambda l:temp_sample(l,0.5),
    'Temp=1.0':lambda l:temp_sample(l,1.0),'Temp=1.5':lambda l:temp_sample(l,1.5),
    'Top-k(5)':lambda l:topk_sample(l,5),'Top-k(20)':lambda l:topk_sample(l,20),
    'Top-p(.8)':lambda l:topp_sample(l,0.8),'Top-p(.95)':lambda l:topp_sample(l,0.95)}
print(f"\\n  {'Strategy':<14} {'Unique':>7} {'Most common':>14}")
print("  "+"-"*40)
for name,fn in strats.items():
    samp=[fn(logits.copy())for _ in range(100)];u=len(set(samp))
    mc=Counter(samp).most_common(1)[0]
    print(f"  {name:<14} {u:>5}     Token {mc[0]}:{mc[1]:>3}x")

print(f"\\n  TEMPERATURE EFFECT ON TOP TOKENS")
print(f"  {'Token':<7}",end="")
for t in[0.3,0.7,1.0,1.5]:print(f"{'T='+str(t):>8}",end="")
print()
for idx in top5[:4]:
    print(f"  #{idx:<5}",end="")
    for t in[0.3,0.7,1.0,1.5]:print(f"{sm(logits/t)[idx]:>8.3f}",end="")
    print()
print(f"\\n  {'Entropy':<7}",end="")
for t in[0.3,0.7,1.0,1.5]:
    p=sm(logits/t);H=-np.sum(p*np.log(p+1e-10));print(f"{H:>8.3f}",end="")
print("  (higher = more random)")

Part 3: Evaluating Generation Quality

How do we know if our model is any good? Three key metrics: Perplexity (exp of average cross-entropy loss — lower is better, 1.0 = perfect), Token Diversity (fraction of unique unigrams and bigrams), and Repetition Rate (how often n-grams repeat — a common LLM failure mode).

Python

np.random.seed(42)

# GENERATION QUALITY EVALUATION
# Reuses model components defined in previous blocks
# ============================================================

        self.blocks=[Bk(d,h,rs)for _ in range(L)];self.ln_f=LN(d);self.head=np.random.randn(d,V)*s;self.V=V;self.T=T

corpus="the cat sat on the mat.\\nthe dog ran in the park.\\nthe model learns to predict.\\nattention helps focus on context.\\ntraining requires data and loss.\\neach layer transforms input.\\npretraining teaches understanding.\\n"*6
tk=CT(corpus);ids_all=tk.encode(corpus);T=32;data=[]
for i in range(0,len(ids_all)-T,10):
    ch=ids_all[i:i+T+1]
    if len(ch)==T+1:data.append((np.array(ch[:-1]),np.array(ch[1:])))
model=GPT(tk.V,64,4,4,T)
for step in range(80):
    idx=np.random.choice(len(data),6);inp=np.stack([data[i][0]for i in idx]);tgt=np.stack([data[i][1]for i in idx])
    lo=model.forward(inp);B,Tl,V=lo.shape;s=lo-lo.max(-1,keepdims=True);p=np.exp(s)/np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
    oh=np.zeros_like(p)

Part 4: Interactive Generation Playground

Experiment with all generation parameters: change temperature, try different prompts, switch strategies.

Partea 2: Strategii de Generare

Un model de limbaj produce o distribuție de probabilitate peste vocabular la fiecare pas. Modul în care alegem un token afectează dramatic calitatea rezultatului. Cele patru strategii principale:

  • Greedy: Alege întotdeauna token-ul cu probabilitatea cea mai mare. Determinist dar adesea repetitiv.
  • Temperature: Împarte logits-urile la T înainte de softmax. T<1 = mai ascuțit (încrezător); T>1 = mai plat (aleatoriu).
  • Top-k: Consideră doar cele mai probabile k token-uri, renormalizează, eșantionează. Previne zgomotul de coadă lungă. Valoare implicită GPT-2: k=40.
  • Top-p (Nucleus): Include cel mai mic set de token-uri a căror probabilitate cumulativă depășește p. Se adaptează dinamic la nivelul de încredere. Implicit în Claude, GPT-4 și majoritatea API-urilor moderne.

Ένα γλωσσικό μοντέλο παράγει μια κατανομή πιθανοτήτων πάνω στο λεξιλόγιο σε κάθε βήμα. Ο τρόπος που επιλέγουμε ένα token επηρεάζει δραματικά την ποιότητα της εξόδου. Οι τέσσερις κύριες στρατηγικές:

  • Greedy: Πάντα επιλέγει το token με την υψηλότερη πιθανότητα. Ντετερμινιστικό αλλά συχνά επαναληπτικό.
  • Temperature: Διαιρεί τα logits με T πριν το softmax. T<1 = πιο οξύ (σίγουρο)· T>1 = πιο επίπεδο (τυχαίο).
  • Top-k: Εξετάζει μόνο τα k πιο πιθανά tokens, επανακανονικοποιεί, δειγματοληπτεί. Αποτρέπει τον θόρυβο μακριάς ουράς. Προεπιλογή GPT-2: k=40.
  • Top-p (Nucleus): Περιλαμβάνει το μικρότερο σύνολο tokens του οποίου η αθροιστική πιθανότητα υπερβαίνει το p. Προσαρμόζεται δυναμικά στο επίπεδο εμπιστοσύνης. Προεπιλογή σε Claude, GPT-4 και τα περισσότερα σύγχρονα APIs.

import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)

# ============================================================
# STAGE 5 CAPSTONE: PRETRAINED TEXT GENERATOR
# ============================================================

class CharTok:
    def __init__(self, text):
        ch = sorted(set(text))
        self.c2i={c:i for i,c in enumerate(ch)}
        self.i2c={i:c for i,c in enumerate(ch)}
        self.V=len(ch)
    def encode(self,t): return [self.c2i.get(c,0) for c in t]
    def decode(self,ids): return ''.join(self.i2c.get(i,'?') for i in ids)

class LN:
    def __init__(self,d):self.g=np.ones(d);self.b=np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self,x):
        mu=x.mean(-1,keepdims=True);v=x.var(-1,keepdims=True)
        return self.g*((x-mu)/np.sqrt(v+1e-5))+self.b
class Attn:
    def __init__(self,d,h,s):
        self.h=h;self.hd=d//h
        self.Wq=np.random.randn(d,d)*s;self.Wk=np.random.randn(d,d)*s
        self.Wv=np.random.randn(d,d)*s;self.Wo=np.random.randn(d,d)*s
    def forward(self,x):
        B,T,C=x.shape;h=self.h;hd=self.hd
        Q=(x@self.Wq).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        K=(x@self.Wk).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        V=(x@self.Wv).reshape(B,T,h,hd).transpose(0,2,1,3)
        sc=Q@K.transpose(0,1,3,2)/np.sqrt(hd)
        sc+=np.triu(np.ones((T,T)),k=1)*(-1e9)
        e=np.exp(sc-sc.max(-1,keepdims=True));a=e/e.sum(-1,keepdims=True)
        return(a@V).transpose(0,2,1,3).reshape(B,T,C)@self.Wo
class FFN:
    def __init__(self,d,s):
        df=4*d;self.W1=np.random.randn(d,df)*s;self.b1=np.zeros(df)
        self.W2=np.random.randn(df,d)*s;self.b2=np.zeros(d)
    def forward(self,x):
        z=x@self.W1+self.b1
        return(0.5*z*(1+np.tanh(np.sqrt(2/np.pi)*(z+0.044715*z**3))))@self.W2+self.b2
class Blk:
    def __init__(self,d,h,s):
        self.ln1=LN(d);self.at=Attn(d,h,s);self.ln2=LN(d);self.ff=FFN(d,s)
    def forward(self,x):
        x=x+self.at.forward(self.ln1.forward(x))
        x=x+self.ff.forward(self.ln2.forward(x));return x
class GPT:
    def __init__(self,V,d,h,L,T):
        s=0.02;rs=s/np.sqrt(2*L)
        self.tok=np.random.randn(V,d)*s;self.pos=np.random.randn(T,d)*s
        self.blocks=[Blk(d,h,rs) for _ in range(L)]
        self.ln_f=LN(d);self.head=np.random.randn(d,V)*s;self.V=V;self.T=T
    def forward(self,ids):
        B,T=ids.shape;x=self.tok[ids]+self.pos[:T]
        for bl in self.blocks:x=bl.forward(x)
        return self.ln_f.forward(x)@self.head

def cross_entropy(logits,targets):
    B,T,V=logits.shape;lf=logits.reshape(B*T,V);tf=targets.reshape(B*T)
    s=lf-lf.max(-1,keepdims=True)
    lp=s-np.log(np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True))
    return -lp[np.arange(B*T),tf].mean()

def train_step(model,inp,tgt,lr):
    logits=model.forward(inp);loss=cross_entropy(logits,tgt)
    B,T,V=logits.shape
    s=logits-logits.max(-1,keepdims=True)
    p=np.exp(s)/np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
    oh=np.zeros_like(p)
    for b in range(B):
        for t in range(T):oh[b,t,tgt[b,t]]=1.0
    dl=(p-oh)/(B*T)
    x=model.tok[inp]+model.pos[:T]
    for bl in model.blocks:x=bl.forward(x)
    x=model.ln_f.forward(x)
    dh=np.zeros_like(model.head)
    for b in range(B):dh+=x[b].T@dl[b]
    gn=np.sqrt((dh**2).sum())
    if gn>1:dh/=gn
    model.head-=lr*dh
    de=np.zeros_like(model.tok);dx=dl@model.head.T
    for b in range(B):
        for t in range(T):de[inp[b,t]]+=dx[b,t]
    en=np.sqrt((de**2).sum())
    if en>1:de/=en
    model.tok-=lr*de
    return loss

# === TRAINING CORPUS ===
corpus = """the cat sat on the mat and looked around the room.
the dog ran in the park and played with the ball.
a bird flew over the tree and sang a beautiful song.
the sun shone brightly in the clear blue sky today.
the model learns to predict the next word in text.
a neural network processes data through many layers.
the attention mechanism helps focus on important parts.
training a language model requires lots of text data.
the transformer block combines attention and feed forward.
each layer builds on the output of the previous one.
the loss function measures how well the model predicts.
gradient descent updates weights to reduce the total loss.
the learning rate controls how big each update step is.
pretraining teaches the model to understand language patterns.
the cat sat on the mat and watched the birds outside.
the dog ran in the park and chased the other dogs.
""" * 4

tok = CharTok(corpus)
ids = tok.encode(corpus)
T = 32
data = []
for i in range(0,len(ids)-T,12):
    ch=ids[i:i+T+1]
    if len(ch)==T+1:data.append((np.array(ch[:-1]),np.array(ch[1:])))

model = GPT(tok.V, d=64, h=4, L=4, T=T)
print("=" * 58)
print("  CAPSTONE: PRETRAINING MINI GPT-2")
print("=" * 58)
print(f"  Vocab: {tok.V} | Tokens: {len(ids)} | Examples: {len(data)}")

max_steps=100; bs=8; max_lr=0.005; min_lr=0.0005; warmup=15
losses=[]
for step in range(max_steps):
    idx=np.random.choice(len(data),bs)
    inp=np.stack([data[i][0] for i in idx])
    tgt=np.stack([data[i][1] for i in idx])
    if step<warmup: lr=max_lr*(step+1)/warmup
    else:
        prog=(step-warmup)/max(1,max_steps-warmup)
        lr=min_lr+0.5*(max_lr-min_lr)*(1+np.cos(np.pi*prog))
    loss=train_step(model,inp,tgt,lr)
    losses.append(float(loss))
    if step%20==0 or step==max_steps-1:
        print(f"  Step {step:3d} | Loss: {loss:.4f} | LR: {lr:.6f}")

def gen(prompt,n=60,temp=0.7):
    ids=tok.encode(prompt)
    for _ in range(n):
        ctx=np.array([ids[-T:]])
        logits=model.forward(ctx)[0,-1]/temp
        p=np.exp(logits-logits.max());p/=p.sum()
        ids.append(int(np.random.choice(len(p),p=p)))
    return tok.decode(ids[len(tok.encode(prompt)):])

print(f"\\n  Loss: {losses[0]:.4f} -> {losses[-1]:.4f} ({(1-losses[-1]/losses[0])*100:.1f}% improvement)")
print("\\n  Sample generations:")
for prompt in ["the ", "a ", "the model "]:
    print(f"  '{prompt}' -> '{prompt}{gen(prompt,60,0.6)}'")
print(f"\\n  Model ready for generation experiments!")

def sm(logits):
    s=logits-logits.max();e=np.exp(s);return e/e.sum()
def greedy(lo):return int(np.argmax(lo))
def temp_sample(lo,T=0.8):p=sm(lo/max(T,1e-8));return int(np.random.choice(len(p),p=p))
def topk_sample(lo,k=10,T=0.8):
    sc=lo/max(T,1e-8);top=np.argsort(sc)[-k:];f=np.full_like(sc,-1e9);f[top]=sc[top]
    p=sm(f);return int(np.random.choice(len(p),p=p))
def topp_sample(lo,p_th=0.9,T=0.8):
    p=sm(lo/max(T,1e-8));si=np.argsort(p)[::-1];cs=np.cumsum(p[si])
    cut=np.searchsorted(cs,p_th)+1;ni=si[:cut];np_=p[ni];np_/=np_.sum()
    return int(np.random.choice(ni,p=np_))
